messages:
alex: Quick callout: our edge build started losing generic inference from the Redwood SDK. `Client<T>` generics aren't flowing to `client.request`. Locally `tsc` is fine, but after bundling (esbuild) types are `any`/`unknown`. Any hints?

ravi: we've hit that before. Often it's an exports/types resolution mismatch. Which package entrypoint is esbuild resolving to? The ESM import or CJS require path?

alex: import is `import Client from '@redwood/inference'`. package.json has conditional exports: `".": { "import": "dist/esm/index.js", "require": "dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "dist/index.d.ts" }`. The dist d.ts looks weird: it re-exports generated types and a lot of `export =` usage.

sophia: `export =` in published d.ts can blow up ESM consumers. TS will widen types if declarations don't present method generics. Also bundlers that inline runtime exports can sever the tsc->dts link. Are you bundling the SDK into the single worker file?

alex: yes, single file bundle for Cloudflare. When I mark `@redwood/inference` external the types are preserved. But we want single-file for deploys.

jen: two immediate options: 1) ask SDK to publish a proper ESM d.ts that matches the import path (e.g., `dist/esm/index.d.ts`) instead of a generic `types` top-level that punts, 2) one-off local augmentation in your repo to fix signatures until upstream fixes.

ravi: also check tsconfig: set `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and `importsNotUsedAsValues: 'preserve'`. That sometimes helps modern ESM packages keep type imports intact for bundlers.

alex: tried those. No change after esbuild. Weirdly, VS Code shows the right types after reload but CI compile (tsc) on the built bundle fails.

sophia: VS Code's tsserver caching can differ from CLI resolution. The key here is bundling: esbuild is rewriting the import into a shim which removes the original import site that tsc uses for contextual typing. If you can't externalize, consider keeping a tiny separate types-only build step that runs `tsc` before bundling and fails fast if generics are gone.

jen: for SDK maintainers: ensure dts keeps method generics (e.g., `request<TIn, TOut>(opts: ...)`) and avoid emitting `any` or `export =`. Also include `typesVersions` mappings if you need to support older TS semantics.

alex: filed a bug with a minimal repro that demonstrates bundled vs unbundled behavior. bot-ci: please open an SDK issue and tag DX/ts.

bot-ci: Created issue #4602 on github.com/redwood-inference/sdk: "Bundled edge consumers lose method generics due to d.ts export layout" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4602 :robot_face:

ravi: temporary consumer hacks: 1) module augmentation in your codebase to re-declare correct signatures, 2) small `types.d.ts` in your repo importing `import type` from the package and re-exporting the types so the bundler picks up the link, 3) pin to a patch release with hand-fixed d.ts via patch-package.

sophia: also watch for `typesVersions` or `exports.types` path mismatches. If the package's types path doesn't match the conditional `import` path, TS might fall back to a CJS d.ts that lacks generics. Recommend SDK add `"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts" } }` so resolution is consistent.

jen: long-term ask: SDK CI should include a tiny ESM/edge consumer test that runs `tsc --noEmit` to assert generics survive packaging and a bundle-time smoke test with esbuild. That would have caught this earlier.

alex: for our ship timeline we'll externalize in esbuild and add a prebundle `tsc` check to CI. Will update the SDK issue with the repro and our temporary patch. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
